item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
059
ABPZ20 KNHC 140522
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Oct 13 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located about 100 miles west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico, and on Tropical Storm Trudy, located several hundred miles
south-southeast of Acapulco, Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Trudy are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast/advisories on Tropical Storm Trudy are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Wed Oct 14 2026 
772 
WTPZ31 KNHC 140848
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Trudy Advisory Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 AM CST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
...TRUDY EXPECTED TO BECOME A HURRICANE WITHIN THE NEXT DAY OR SO..
...RESIDENTS OF SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO SHOULD CONTINUE
TO MONITOR THE PROGRESS OF THIS SYSTEM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.1N 99.0W
ABOUT 405 MI...650 KM S OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 650 MI...1045 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico should monitor the
progress of Trudy. Watches will likely be required later today for
portions of these areas.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Trudy was 
located near latitude 11.1 North, longitude 99.0 West. Trudy is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A motion 
between west-northwest and northwest should continue through 
tonight. A turn toward the north-northwest and a decrease in forward 
speed is expected on Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast during the next few 
days, and the cyclone is expected to become a hurricane by tonight 
and a major hurricane by Friday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern Mexico late this week. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 140848
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Trudy Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 AM CST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
Trudy continues to be a complicated storm to locate and forecast. A 
recent ASCAT pass shows that the center is farther west-southwest 
than the previous best track position. In addition, the ASCAT pass 
was also used to adjust the wind radii for the cyclone. The 
satellite presentation shows that the bulk of the convection remains 
on the north side of the storm, but recently new deep convection has 
developed over the center with cloud tops colder than -70 C based 
on the infrared imagery. Based on the latest TAFB Dvorak and 
UW-CIMSS intensity estimates, the initial intensity for Trudy has 
been raised to 45 kt.
 
The repositioning of the center based on the previously mentioned 
ASCAT pass has long-reaching impacts for the track forecast. With 
the initial position farther west-southwest than before, the updated 
track has been generally shifted west of the previous forecast. The 
current track forecast has Trudy being steered by a mid-level ridge 
over the southern United States for the next 72 h. Afterwards, the 
uncertainty in the track becomes larger than normal due to the 
cyclone entering a region of weaker steering flow. This occurs due 
to the previously mentioned mid-level ridge retreating as a trough 
moves over the western United States. The current NHC track 
forecast heavily favors the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids. In this 
current track forecast, the center of the cyclone does remain 
offshore of southwestern Mexico, but there is still a lot of 
uncertainty regarding the long-range track forecast.
 
The environmental conditions are very favorable for strengthening, 
and Trudy is expected to rapidly intensify and should become a 
hurricane within 24 h. Trudy is forecast to reach major hurricane 
status somewhere around 48 h and continue to intensify for around 
60-72 h. After that, wind shear is expected to steadily increase as 
mid-level relative humidity decreases, thus a general weakening 
trend is expected to occur. The new intensity forecast is generally 
about the same as the previous one, however slower weakening is 
shown late in the period since the new forecast remains offshore. 
The current intensity forecast is still on the upper end of the 
guidance envelope, but is in good agreement with HCCA and GDMI 
forecast aids.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico late this week and
into the weekend. There is an increasing risk of wind, rain, and
storm surge impacts, and watches could be required for a portion of
these areas later today.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  14/0900Z 11.1N  99.0W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  14/1800Z 11.5N 100.2W   55 KT  65 MPH
 24H  15/0600Z 12.4N 101.3W   65 KT  75 MPH

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 28
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 140845
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  28
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
...COMPACT SIMON DRIFTING SOUTHWESTWARD...
...INTERESTS IN WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO AND BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD
CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.8N 107.9W
ABOUT 150 MI...240 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 150 MI...245 KM SW OF LAS ISLAS MARIAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...105 MPH...165 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 230 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...969 MB...28.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in west-central Mexico and in Baja California Sur should
continue to monitor Simon. Additional watches or warnings may be
required over the next day or two.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 19.8 North, longitude 107.9 West. Simon is moving 
toward the southwest near 3 mph (6 km/h). The hurricane could move 
slowly and erratically during the next day or two. An eventual turn 
toward the north or north-northwest is forecast to occur by Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 105 mph (165 km/h)
with higher gusts. Some intensity fluctuations are possible during
the next couple of days, followed by weakening on Friday and into
the weekend.
 
Simon is a very small hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend
outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the center, and
tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 969 mb (28.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are possible within the hurricane watch
area for Las Islas Marias on Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Through Friday, Simon is expected to produce rainfall
totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3 inches
over portions of the states of Baja California Sur, Nayarit, and
Sinaloa.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 500 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 28
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 140846
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  28
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Wed Oct 14 2026
 
Proxy-visible and infrared satellite images of Simon show the tiny
eye of the hurricane has filled during the past few hours. There has
also been a warming of the inner core cloud tops, and the central
dense overcast has become less symmetric. These changes could be the
result of some northerly shear affecting Simon as diagnosed by
UW-CIMSS. There is no recent passive microwave data available to
assess the internal structure of Simon, but recent scatterometer
data and distant radar data from Los Cabos indicate that the
hurricane remains very small. The initial intensity is lowered
slightly to 90 kt, in best agreement with the latest Dvorak CI
number (5.0) from TAFB and an earlier 88-kt D-MINT estimate.
 
The hurricane is moving slowly southwestward (230/3 kt). In the near 
term, Simon is expected to remain within very weak steering 
currents. Thus, it is likely to meander well offshore of 
west-central Mexico during the next couple of days, with the model 
consensus generally favoring a slow southwestward or southward 
motion through Thursday. From there, the future track will depend on 
the vertical depth of Simon and its interaction with an upper-level 
trough over the western United States. This feature should cause 
Simon to turn northward at some point, but there is large spread 
among the track models as to when and where this turn occurs. There 
has been a substantial westward shift in the long-range track 
guidance, with almost all models now bringing Simon near or west of 
the Baja California Peninsula at 72-120 h. The NHC forecast has been 
adjusted in the direction of the latest multi-model consensus to 
reflect this trend, but future adjustments will likely be required.
 
Simon's small size makes it susceptible to intensity fluctuations 
based on the state of its compact inner core and small changes in 
the environmental conditions. The hurricane is forecast to drift 
over very warm waters in a fairly weak shear environment during the 
next day or two. However, the mid-level environmental humidity is 
only around 50 percent, and even slightly stronger shear than 
forecast could disrupt the core and induce some weakening. The 
official NHC forecast shows little net change in the next 24-36 h, 
recognizing that some of the hurricane regional models show another 
round of strengthening could occur during this period. There is 
higher confidence that the aforementioned trough will impart 
stronger vertical wind shear over Simon by Friday, which should 
induce a steady weakening trend through the weekend.
 
Simon continues to be a challenging storm to forecast, and
confidence remains lower than normal given the weak steering,
proximity to land, very small size, and significant model spread.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon could be near Las Islas Marias on Thursday, where a
Hurricane Watch remains in effect. Interests in west-central Mexico
and Baja California Sur should continue to closely monitor the
latest updates. Additional watches or warnings could be required
over the next day or two.
 
2. Large swells will likely affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur over the next several
days. These swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.
